newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco invites five bidders for $300 mln port.
newsitem.headline: Morocco invites five bidders for $300 mln port.

text.p: Morocco is inviting five foreign consortiums to tender on September 15 to build a $300 million port in the northern city of Tangier, a public works ministry spokesman said on Friday.

The consortiums, which have been subject to a preliminary selection, are Bechtel-ICTSI of the United States, France's GTM-Entrepose, Bouygues -CMA-Bymaro and Campenon Bernard-SGTM-Dredging Int-Entracanales Y Tavora, and the Spanish company Dragados-FCC.
The port which will be located about 20 km (12 miles) south of Tangier, will ease congestion on the existing port and create an infrastructure for external trade.
The spokesman said the site of the new port was on a deeper harbour area which could accommodate ships of greater tonnage than the existing port.
Tangier port last year handled 1.9 million tonnes of freight and 1,451,000 passengers.
"The future port will become a trans-shipment centre which will at the same time ease congestion of the present port," the spokesman said.
The successful tenderer will finance construction of the port and in turn be granted a long-term concession to run it. The length of this had yet to be negotiated.
"It is the first time in Morocco's port infrastructure that financing through concession has been used," he said.
The successful bidder would also have the possibility of a concession to take over management of the existing port.
